StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Single and the sim leaves Power.on_stack alone, so it adds -- which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236, no StackType branch). This is the CORRECT handling of Single; the census's 15 wrong units are the ones that override on_stack to `pass` (`py audit/tools/power_census.py stack`). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

InstanceType.rationale: CLOSED 2026-08-01 (entity-obs-schema phase 0). The `stolen_cards` LIST this entry recorded is gone: SwipePower declares PowerInstanceType.INSTANCED and holds exactly one `stolen_card`, so each steal arms its own power, matching SwipePower.cs:17/:23/:25-35. The bundling existed only because `Creature.powers` was a dict with one slot per id, which would have orphaned every steal but the last; it is `creatures.PowerList` now, C#'s ordered `List<PowerModel>`. The three readers moved with it: the hopper's steal takes the instance `PowerCmd.apply` returns (mirroring `Apply<T>`, PowerCmd.cs:66-87) instead of a lookup by id, and both the escape hand-off (monsters/hive/thieving_hopper.py) and `RunState.finish_combat`'s deck reconciliation (run.py) walk `powers.instances("swipe")` -- C#'s GetPowerInstances -- instead of the single dict slot, which is the reachability this entry's own DORMANT reasoning depended on. C#'s per-instance `Target` is still unmodelled; that is the single-player narrowing recorded on the Steal guard, not an instancing gap. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

BeforeDeath.issue: HOOK SLOT: C# is `BeforeDeath`, fired at CreatureCmd.cs:503 **before** `Hook.ShouldDie` and therefore before any death prevention; the sim uses `hooks.on_death`, fired at cmds.py:105 only on the branch where should_die returned True. Two consequences. (1) A PREVENTED death fires C#'s BeforeDeath and not the sim's on_death, so the game would queue the stolen card's reward for a hopper that did not actually die and the sim would not. (2) Ordering: in C# the reward is queued before the death resolves, so anything the death triggers sees it already present. DORMANT: the only owner is the ported Thieving Hopper (monsters/hive/thieving_hopper.py), which carries no death-prevention power -- it has EscapeArtist and Flutter, neither of which implements should_die -- so should_die is always True for it and BeforeDeath and on_death coincide. Trigger: an Illusion / Adaptable / Reattach / SteamEruption holder that also holds Swipe. The sim's docstring is right about the harder half of this hook -- BeforeDeath fires "only when the *owner* dies, never on escape" -- because Escape is not a Kill. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: powers.py:2271-2273 skips any stolen card with no `combat.deck_card_origins` entry, which is the sim's DeckVersion analogue and is documented as such (powers.py:2245-2247). A combat-only copy never comes back on either side.

guards.what: SwipePower.cs:61-64 AddCard + SpecialCardReward on the CombatRoom
guards.rationale: powers.py:2269-2273 appends a RewardExtra.of_card(origin) to `combat.pending_reward_extras`. C# additionally calls `runState.AddCard(...)` FIRST and then queues the reward as a take-or-skip; the sim queues only the reward. Recorded as faithful because the C# AddCard is immediately followed by a SpecialCardReward for the same card, i.e. the deck add is the reward's payload, and the sim models the whole thing as one pending reward.
Run-history bookkeeping for the map screen; presentation.

guards.what: SwipePower.cs:69-78 Steal(card) removing the card from the run deck
guards.rationale: The sim's steal path is the hopper's, not this power's; this power only holds the list. Recorded so a reader knows the public non-override method was seen -- like CrueltyPower.ModifyVulnerableMultiplier, it is not a hook and the harness does not enumerate it.

Closed game-wide, re-verified 2026-07-26. EXECUTED: `py audit/tools/power_census.py visible` reports 0 IsVisibleInternal overrides of 260 files. That 260 is the .cs files DIRECTLY under src/Core/Models/Powers and EXCLUDES the 16 in Powers/Mocks/ (276 including them); a recursive `grep -rn IsVisibleInternal src/Core/Models/Powers/`, which does cover Mocks/, also returns 0 -- so IsVisible is provably always true for every power in the decompiled game, mocks included. CITATION FIX (2026-07-26 review fix pass): the property lives in src/Core/Models/PowerModel.cs, NOT under Models/Powers/ -- `IsVisible` is the non-virtual property at PowerModel.cs:150-160 and the overridable virtual is `IsVisibleInternal` at PowerModel.cs:167.
